jsc.cli.man.afterboot.about.3: syspatch installs the system's own patches from the Mirror, which syspatch -c lists first; /etc/pf.conf holds the firewall's rules, which pfctl -si reports on; and doas runs a command as another user.

jsc.cli.man.apropos.summary: search what every command is for

jsc.cli.man.info.about.keys: n, p and u go to the next node, the previous one and the one above it; l goes back. Tab picks a link and Enter follows it. m goes to a menu item by name and s searches the manual. h shows the keys and q leaves.

jsc.cli.man.intro.about.2: man <command> opens any of their pages; apropos <word> searches every page this machine has for that word; whatis <command> gives the one line a page opens with, which is enough to tell whether it is worth reading at all.
jsc.cli.man.intro.summary: introduction to the commands run at a shell prompt
jsc.cli.man.listcmd.about: Lists every command this computer offers and every program installed on it, in one list, whichever system it runs. Nothing here is hidden and nothing is added: it is the same answer the prompt itself gives when it decides whether a word is a command.
jsc.cli.man.listcmd.summary: list everything this computer can run
jsc.cli.man.whatis.about: Prints the one line a manual page opens with, which is enough to tell whether the page is worth opening at all.
jsc.cli.man.whatis.summary: say in one line what a command is for

jsc.configuration.boot.show_boot_menu.to:

Turning this off boots the chosen system at once, the way a machine with the menu hidden does.
jsc.configuration.boot.tooltip: How the machines come up: whether they stop at their system's boot manager.
jsc.configuration.client.desktop_cursors: Whether the desktops draw their own pointer over the monitor's glass: each system's arrow, and its hourglass, ring or watch while it is busy. Off, the game's own pointer stays.
jsc.configuration.client.notifications_o: Whether the network's alerts to the portable devices this player carries show on the HUD too, as J's Core's notifications at the attention level, naming the device they came from. Off, they reach the device alone.
jsc.configuration.client.outside_compone:
Whether this game draws the components of programs' windows that reach outside the game, such as one showing a web address or a file on this computer.
Off, each shows a placeholder naming it, whatever the server allows.
jsc.configuration.client.tooltip: How the desktops look on this game: whose pointer they draw, and what of the world outside the game they show; and whether the portables' alerts show on the HUD.
Whether power supplies wear out while they are on and in the end fail, faster the nearer their rating they run: degraded from 80% worn, with warnings at every boot, and failed at 100%, when the computer shuts down and does not start until the supply is replaced.
Off, no supply wears, warns or fails.
jsc.configuration.hardware.psu_life_mult: How much longer than their lines' lives every power supply lasts: 2 is twice as long, 0.5 half.
jsc.configuration.hardware.tooltip: How the parts age: the power supplies' wear and their failure.
jsc.configuration.install_by_hand.arch_e:
Whether installing Arch by hand asks for every step of the installation guide.
Off, only the steps a system cannot boot without are asked for. On, the hardware clock and a name for the machine are asked for as well.
jsc.configuration.install_by_hand.gentoo:
Whether installing Gentoo by hand asks for every step of the handbook.
Off, only the steps a system cannot boot without are asked for: the disk, the stage 3, the package tree, a kernel, the filesystem table and the bootloader.
On, the rest are asked for as well: the bind mounts, a profile, the @world update, the kernel link and a name for the machine.
Every step answers the way the real tool does either way; this only decides which of them a restart refuses to go on without.
jsc.configuration.install_by_hand.toolti: Installing a system by hand: how much of its guide the machine insists on.
jsc.configuration.item_loss.corruption.t:
Whether storage can be corrupted at all: by a network conflict, or by a thermal trip, which may corrupt the disks of the machine that shut down. Corrupted items leave the network's index until the Defrag gives them back or loses them.
Off, nothing is ever corrupted.
jsc.configuration.item_loss.network_conf:
Whether a network conflict, two Mainframes on one network, costs: what the discarded Operations were carrying is lost, and a tenth of what both networks store is corrupted, waiting for the Defrag.
Off, a conflict gives everything back and corrupts nothing.
jsc.configuration.item_loss.network_spli:
Whether what an Operation was carrying is lost when the network splits under it: a cable pulled between the Mainframe and a server it was reading or writing, a router that disappears.
Off, the Operation stops and gives everything back.
jsc.configuration.item_loss.power_loss.t:
Whether what the Operations were carrying is lost when the machine running them goes dark suddenly: a power loss, unstable power or a power supply failing. The log says how much and of what.
Off, a sudden shutdown gives everything back, as switching the machine off does.
jsc.configuration.item_loss.tooltip: What a player who lets the network fail pays for it: the items in transit, lost in each situation turned on here.
jsc.configuration.power.draw_energy.tool:
Whether the computers draw energy for what their parts take, through their power supplies: J's Energy in the low voltage class, or FE where J's Core lets the series take it. A computer without it does not start, and one that loses it goes dark.
Off, every computer runs free, and so do the chain's benches and machines, for a world with no energy source at all.
jsc.configuration.power.tooltip: What the computers run on: the energy their power supplies draw.
jsc.configuration.printing.enchanted_boo:
Whether the Large Scale Printer prints enchanted books from the .ench files scanners make, each with every enchantment at the level it was scanned with.
Off, it refuses them and says why, for a world where every enchantment is earned.
jsc.configuration.programs.outside_compo:
Whether a program may put in its windows a component of a kind that reaches outside the game, such as one showing a web address or a file on the player's own computer.
Such kinds come only from other mods, which say so when they add them. Off, a program making one is stopped and told; on, each player still sees them only if their own settings turn them on as well.
jsc.configuration.programs.tooltip: What the programs players write may put in their windows.
jsc.configuration.prompt.list_commands.t:
Whether every computer has the 'listcmd' command, which lists absolutely everything that computer can run right now: its commands, whatever family they belong to, and the programs installed on it.
Off, it is nowhere at all: not in help, not in a manual, not in what a half-typed name completes to, and typing it is an unknown command. Each system then teaches what it has in its own way, which is the experience those systems really gave.
On, it is on every computer and shows up everywhere like any other command, for whoever would rather read one list than learn each system's own habits.
